\chapter{Graph Theory — Optimality}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.GraphTheory.Kruskal.Optimality
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Overview}

This chapter establishes the correctness and optimality of Kruskal's algorithm on a
weighted edge list over the vertex set $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$: the greedy loop
$\texttt{Kruskal.processEdges}$ preserves the connectivity partition of its input, and the
resulting edge set $\texttt{Kruskal.kruskal}$ spans exactly what the input spans while
having minimum total weight among all spanning subsets of the input.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Union--find state after the greedy loop]
\lean{Kruskal.ufAfterProcessEdges}
\label{Kruskal.ufAfterProcessEdges}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.UF, Kruskal.UF.find, Kruskal.UF.merge, Kruskal.WEdge}
The union--find structure obtained by running the greedy loop over a list of weighted
edges: starting from a state $uf$, each edge $e$ is merged into the state when its
endpoints $e.u$ and $e.v$ currently lie in different components, and is ignored
otherwise. Unlike $\texttt{Kruskal.processEdges}$ it returns only the final state, not the
list of accepted edges.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Greedy loop induces the full merge partition]
\lean{Kruskal.ufAfterProcessEdges_partition}
\label{Kruskal.ufAfterProcessEdges_partition}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.UF, Kruskal.UF.SamePartition, Kruskal.UF.merge, Kruskal.UF.mergeAll, Kruskal.WEdge, Kruskal.merge_noop, Kruskal.ufAfterProcessEdges}
For every edge list and every initial state $uf$, the state
$\texttt{Kruskal.ufAfterProcessEdges}$ produces induces the same partition of the vertices
as merging all the edges unconditionally, i.e.\ it has the same partition as
$uf.\mathrm{mergeAll}$ applied to the whole list.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Accumulator factors out of the greedy loop]
\lean{Kruskal.processEdges_acc}
\label{Kruskal.processEdges_acc}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.UF, Kruskal.UF.merge, Kruskal.WEdge, Kruskal.processEdges}
Running $\texttt{Kruskal.processEdges}$ with an accumulator $acc$ yields
$acc^{\mathrm{rev}}$ followed by the output of the same run started from the empty
accumulator; the accumulator only contributes a reversed prefix.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Selected edges span the same partition]
\lean{Kruskal.processEdges_same_partition}
\label{Kruskal.processEdges_same_partition}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.UF, Kruskal.UF.SamePartition, Kruskal.UF.find, Kruskal.UF.mergeAll, Kruskal.WEdge, Kruskal.processEdges, Kruskal.processEdges_acc, Kruskal.ufAfterProcessEdges, Kruskal.ufAfterProcessEdges_partition}
Merging the edges selected by the greedy loop into $uf$ gives the same partition as
merging all the input edges into $uf$: the discarded edges never change connectivity.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Skipping an edge inside a component]
\lean{Kruskal.processEdges_skip}
\label{Kruskal.processEdges_skip}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.UF, Kruskal.UF.find, Kruskal.WEdge, Kruskal.processEdges}
If the endpoints of $e$ already have the same union--find representative, then the
greedy loop on $e :: rest$ from state $uf$ returns exactly the output of the loop on
$rest$ from the same state.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Weight contributed by an accepted edge]
\lean{Kruskal.processEdges_take_weight}
\label{Kruskal.processEdges_take_weight}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.UF, Kruskal.UF.find, Kruskal.UF.merge, Kruskal.WEdge, Kruskal.processEdges, Kruskal.processEdges_acc, Kruskal.totalWeight}
If the endpoints of $e$ lie in different components of $uf$, then the total weight of the
greedy output on $e :: rest$ equals $e.\mathrm{weight}$ plus the total weight of the
greedy output on $rest$ started from the merged state $uf.\mathrm{merge}\,e.u\,e.v$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Optimality of the greedy edge-selection loop]
\lean{Kruskal.processEdges_optimal}
\label{Kruskal.processEdges_optimal}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.Reach, Kruskal.UF, Kruskal.UF.SamePartition, Kruskal.UF.SamePartition.symm, Kruskal.UF.SamePartition.trans, Kruskal.UF.find, Kruskal.UF.merge, Kruskal.UF.mergeAll, Kruskal.WEdge, Kruskal.erase_append_perm, Kruskal.mergeAll_cons_eq, Kruskal.mergeAll_iff_reach, Kruskal.mergeAll_perm, Kruskal.merge_noop, Kruskal.processEdges, Kruskal.processEdges_skip, Kruskal.processEdges_take_weight, Kruskal.reduce_to_rest, Kruskal.totalWeight, Kruskal.totalWeight_erase, Kruskal.uf_exchange}
Let $uf$ be a union--find state whose classes are exactly the reachability classes of a
base edge list, and let the input list $edges$ be sorted by nondecreasing weight. Then
for any competing sublist $S \subseteq edges$ that induces the same partition as $edges$
does over $uf$, the greedy output satisfies
\[
  \mathrm{totalWeight}\bigl(\mathrm{processEdges}\;edges\;uf\;[\,]\bigr)
  \;\le\; \mathrm{totalWeight}(S).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Kruskal's output spans the input]
\lean{Kruskal.kruskal_spans}
\label{Kruskal.kruskal_spans}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.Reach, Kruskal.SpansLike, Kruskal.UF.init, Kruskal.WEdge, Kruskal.kruskal, Kruskal.mergeAll_init_iff, Kruskal.processEdges_same_partition, Kruskal.reach_mono}
For every weighted edge list $E$ over $\mathrm{Fin}\,n$, the output $\mathrm{kruskal}\,n\,E$
spans like $E$: any two vertices reachable in $E$ are reachable using only the selected
edges.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Optimality of Kruskal's algorithm]
\lean{Kruskal.kruskal_optimal}
\label{Kruskal.kruskal_optimal}
\leanok
\uses{Kruskal.SpansLike, Kruskal.WEdge, Kruskal.kruskal, Kruskal.mergeAll_init_iff, Kruskal.processEdges_optimal, Kruskal.reach_mono, Kruskal.totalWeight}
If $S$ is a sublist of $E$ that spans like $E$, then
\[
  \mathrm{totalWeight}\bigl(\mathrm{kruskal}\;n\;E\bigr) \;\le\; \mathrm{totalWeight}(S),
\]
so Kruskal's output has minimum total weight among all spanning subsets of $E$.
\end{theorem}
